input: Apply for a remote work visa in Costa Rica

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: The user may need help with the full end-to-end process (researching eligibility, gathering documents, submitting the application, arriving in-country) or just one specific part of it, which completely changes the scope of the plan.
Whether the application is just for the user or also includes dependents (spouse, children) significantly changes the required documents and fees.
The user's current country of residence affects which Costa Rican consulate they must apply through, whether they apply from abroad or in-country, and applicable processing timelines.

Costa Rica's Digital Nomad Visa requires proof of a minimum monthly income (currently ~$3,000/month). Knowing the user's employment type (employee vs. freelancer) determines which income documents are needed.
The user may want to apply online, through a local Costa Rican immigration lawyer, or via a consulate in their home country — each has different steps, costs, and timelines.
Some users want to move as fast as possible; others want to be thorough and avoid mistakes. This affects whether the plan prioritises speed, accuracy, or cost-efficiency.
The user's end goal — short stay vs. long-term residency, single entry vs. multiple entries — determines which visa category is actually the right fit and what 'done' looks like.

gold.taskTitle: Apply for Costa Rica Remote Work Visa
gold.taskDescription: The user wants to apply for Costa Rica's Digital Nomad Visa (Rentista/Remote Worker visa), which allows foreign nationals to live and work remotely in Costa Rica for foreign-based employers or clients.

questions.title: Which part of the process do you need help with?
questions.description: Does the user need a full step-by-step plan (research through approval), or help with a specific stage such as document preparation or the submission form?

questions.title: Will you be applying for dependents too?
questions.description: Is this application for the user alone, or does it include a spouse or children who need to be listed as dependents on the visa?

questions.title: What country are you currently living in?
questions.description: The user's current country of residence determines the relevant Costa Rican consulate, language requirements for documents, and whether they apply abroad or inside Costa Rica.

questions.title: Are you a salaried employee or a freelancer/self-employed?
questions.description: Costa Rica requires proof of stable income above a monthly threshold; the exact documents differ significantly between employees (pay stubs, employer letter) and freelancers (contracts, bank statements).

questions.title: Do you plan to use an immigration lawyer or apply independently?
questions.description: Choosing between a Costa Rican immigration attorney, a visa agency, or a self-guided application changes the steps, cost, and level of support built into the plan.

questions.title: How soon do you need the visa approved?
questions.description: The user's timeline (e.g., moving in 2 months vs. 6 months) determines whether to prioritise speed, use expedited services, or take a more thorough and cost-effective approach.

questions.title: Are you looking to stay short-term or establish long-term residency?
questions.description: Whether the user wants a temporary digital nomad visa (1–2 years) or is aiming toward permanent residency changes which visa category is the right target and what the final success state looks like.
